letrong giap.name: Letrong Giap
letrong giap.origin: In 1954, Giap was a Captain in the Viet Minh, serving in the 13th Infantry Regiment of the 199th Signals Company. He led his men against the French military forces occupying Vietnam and it was during this time that he encountered Nick Fury who was part of a CIA mission to help the French hold the territory. Giap's men were successful in killing the French forces Fury was allied with. At this point, Fury, heavily concussed and disoriented from the battle, was told by Giap that Vietnam does not belong to the French or to the United States and was allowed to leave peacefully, perhaps to spread the message to his superiors in the CIA. Fury would next encounter Giap in 1970. By this time, Giap was a North Vietnamese Army General known for defeating U.S. forces time and again. Fury was dispatched on a mission to assassinate Giap with the aid of U.S. Marine sniper Frank Castle. Unfortunately for Fury, Giap's men discovered him and Castle and imprisoned them. Giap planned to link the CIA to drugs being moved into Vietnam from Cambodia; the resulting backlash would end the war much quicker. Fury and Castle escape, with Castle grabbing his rifle and picking off scores of Giap's men from a hilltop. Fury himself goes after Giap, but is held at gunpoint. Giap questions why Fury would want to prolong such a horrible war, but before any kind of understanding is met, Castle shoots Giap through the neck, apparently killing him. His base of operations was later bombed by U.S. Air Force jets, with Fury and Castle barely escaping in time. Miraculously, Giap survived the bullet to the neck and the bombing, but was put in a coma for a month. In 1999, after attending the Smithsonian's Conference on Cold War Historical Studies in Washington D.C., he would greet Fury at the Vietnam War Memorial. Giap discussed the aftermath of the war with Fury, stating that although America lost in Vietnam, it did not become the prosperous country they hoped it would be under communism. He told Fury that despite sacrificing so much of his humanity to wage war, it ultimately did not pay off the way he hoped it would. Giap shakes Fury's hand, wishing him the best. Author Michael Goodwin met Giap at either the 1999 conference or another Smithsonian conference which inspired Goodwin to think about writing his first book. After his book Valley Forge, Valley Forge was published in the 00's, Goodwin interviewed Giap to get his (and North Vietnam's side) of the war, to understand why circumstances would create The Punisher, and in turn his interview with Giap prompted Goodwin to interview the remaining members of Frank Castle's first command. ==Personality== Giap was a skilled strategist and a great leader to his men, leading them to victory over American forces time after time. He was a patriotic man, resenting the French and American governments for thinking they had a right to control Vietnam. He believed that Vietnam should be a strong, independent nation free of foreign political influence. Despite his role as a soldier, he was not fond of war. He explains to Fury that the war has made him do many horrible things that he regrets, but that he did those things in the hopes that it would benefit his country. In his later life, Giap became somewhat disillusioned with his country as Vietnam never became the worker's paradise that communism promised. Instead, he feels it became every bit as brutal to its own people in peacetime as it was to its enemies in war.

lettre a cell combattre.origin: Lettre A was a member of Cell Combattre, a violent Quebec separatist movement. levi weinlaub.origin: Levi Weinlaub was a young Jewish boy in Warsaw during WWII. One night, he, Max Eisenhardt and Avner were smuggling food for their families. When they got to a wall, Max and Levi got through it, but Avner was caught by Nazi soldiers before he could pass. Herr Hitzig falsely offered Avner the chance to get his family fresh food in exchange for the names of the people who had gone with him. Avner gave him the name of Levi. From the other side of the wall, Max and Levi were listening what was happening. Max told Levi to go warn his family, and that was the last he saw of him.

leviagod.name: Leviagod
leviagod.species: God; possibly Undergod or Dark One (see notes)
leviagod.origin: The Leviagod, also known as the Dark One, the God Below, the Undergod, was a giant god. Using avalanches in the mountains of Ghulistan, sand pits in the desert of Kara Korum, earthquakes in the Himelians, caves in the Hyrkanian Mountains. People trapped in the belly of the Undergod were eventually (sometimes after years) turned into the Leech-Men, mindless slaves devoted to protecting the caves of the Undergod. The sane humans were assaulted by Leech-Men, deceased entrapped people manifesting as memories. The Undergod also clouded their minds, causing memory losses. Born there, the White Witch, the Lady Liv, guided the entrapped travelers, as her "people". Conan was trapped in an avalanche in the mountains of Ghulistan. He was saved by the White Witch and people, and he agreed to help them slay the Undergod. To Conan, the Leech-Men took the form of Thak, the Frost Giant brothers of Atali, Ghost Snakes, Sschaaronn, the Man-Serpent, the Dragon of Xuchotl, the snake-faced children of Set, the man-eating spiders of Zamora, the deformed Sea Beasts from the Ship of the Deed, Yag-Kosha, the Swamp Devil child of Jhebbal Sag, the winged horror that slew Bêlit, and the Night-Cult. Finally, the group arrived at the Grotto of Blood. There, Conan had to defeat a foe unknown to him, Razazel. Conan defeated Razazel by drowning him in the Undergod's blood, killed the Leviagod in the process, and causing to burst out of the mountain, and letting free the entrapped people.

leviathan whalesong.name: Leviathan (Whalesong)
leviathan whalesong.species: Mythical Sea Creature (resembled a colossal squid)
leviathan whalesong.origin: ===Origins=== Leviathan is a giant sea beast who was for some reason watching over a young half-Atlantean woman unaware of her heritage, now known as Whalesong. Being caught in a boating accident, she nearly died, only to be saved by the Leviathan. Developing a bond with the creature, she took to living inside it. At some point in time she started attending the University of Atlantis before Wakandan forces attacked the city. ===Infinity=== When the Wakandan Hatut Zeraze, then Thanos' forces invaded, Whalesong somehow avoided being attacked until the students from the other Super Human schools arrived to try and fight them. Being beaten back, Whalesong called upon Leviathan to swallow the teens in order to save them. After finding that Thanos' army is heading to Wakanda, Demona used her powers to teleport Leviathan and everyone inside it to Wakanda. Engaging the enemy, a massive monster amongst Thanos' forces attacked only to be met by Leviathan. Despite its best efforts however, Leviathan was beaten badly, leaving Whalesong mourning the injury to her gigantic guardian. After fighting off the attack, the Wakandans managed to get Leviathan back into the ocean where it healed quickly.

leviathon mother.origin: The Leviathon Mother was the matriarch of the Leviathon Tide, and mother of the Leviathons and Leviathon Servitors, who launched an invasion of Earth from the Desecrated Nest. After being noticed of the high level of resistance found in this planet, the Leviathon Mother made earthfall herself and called out the individual behind the strongest line of defense, a young Inhuman named Kei Kawade who had the ability to summon monsters independent from the Tide, the Goliathons, to fight on his behalf against the invading forces. thumb|left|Smasher defeating the Leviathon Mother The Leviathon Mother was confronted by Kei soon after she defeated the heroes and the Goliathons. The young boy pushed the boundaries of his powers and used them to summon entirely new monsters of his own creation. These six new monsters managed to fend off the Leviathon Mother until she killed one of them, Fireclaw. Kei used his abilities to merge the remaining monsters and himself into a creature named Smasher. Smasher turned the tide of the battle in Kei's favor, and eventually killed the Leviathon Mother. The body subsequently melted.

Cracking, Lew fled to the basement and activated an electrical switchboard connected to explosives. Hurricane landed a lethal blow, killing Lew. Then he, his sidekick Speedy, and Florence got out of the house before it exploded.

lewis green.name: Lewis Green
lewis green.species: Human empowered by the Amulet of Achilles
lewis green.origin: Hired by the mysterious General to retrieve an object of power from the ancient ruins of Troy in modern-day Turkey, Lewis Green put his life on hold (including his engagement) to do the man's bidding. Spending weeks searching for the object, he eventually discovered it (partially thanks to the workings of Greek goddess Nox) and returned to America. Escorted home by the General's men, he immediately left home to see his fiancée, only to discover her living with another man. Scared off by the much-larger man, he left to await his meeting with the General. Upon meeting with the General, he was informed of the power of the item he held (the Amulet of Achilles), and that the General intended to kill him to keep his acquiring of the object a secret. Taking out his gun and firing on Green, he instead hit the Amulet Green was holding, knocking Green off the roof and activating the Amulet, transforming Green into the new Achilles, imbuing him with a protective field, a golden shield, and a large sword. Knowing that for every man he killed he would gain a year of life, he sought out the man his former fiancée was now married to, intent on freeing her from his clutches. Attacking the man, he found himself stopped by the woman, who informed Green of her love for the man and telling Green he was clearly insane. Vowing vengeance on the General, Green then went in search of the man. Following an unsuccessful assault on the General and Nox, Achilles and his allies (Surgeon, Operative, Aviatrix, and Revenant) made one final assault on the General in order to stop the sacrifice of a group of children. Lending his sword to the Operative during the assault so the man could defeat the General, Achilles then harnessed all of the absorbed life energy he'd gained over the weeks of tracking the General to assault and defeat Nox, killing himself in the process.
powers: The Amulet of Achilles causes a golden aura to surround him, greatly his endurance.
abilities: Master .
weapons: Large sword and golden shield.
weaknesses: For every day he uses the Amulet, a year of his life is lost, but for every man he kills wearing the Amulet, he gains a year of life.

lewis hammond.name: Lewis Hammond
lewis hammond.origin: The population of Almost Reno, New Mexico, was rendered sterile by atomic tests. In an effort to control mutant-kind, Odysseus Indigo's Damocles Foundation approached them, and offered to return their ability to have children. The Damocles Foundation injected the townspeople with both mutant and deviant DNA, which restored their fertility and ensured that any of their children would be born superhuman, and thus ideal test subjects for Indigo. One of these children was Lewis Hammond, who radiated a red glow at all times. He was the first of the Foundation's children to destabilize, as he rapidly began glowing brighter and brighter; within the course of a single school period, he was so bright that no one could look at him.
powers: Lewis perpetually radiated a type of red, glowing energy from his body. Upon the destabilization of his powers, his glow became so bright that it was painful to look upon.

lewis haywerth.name: Lewis Haywerth
lewis haywerth.origin: ===Early Years=== Lewis Haywerth enlisted in the U.S. Army at a young age and advanced steadily through the ranks, earning a reputation for disciplined command, procurement savvy, and interagency coordination. His staff postings expanded from unit logistics to theater level planning, where he liaised with intelligence services and defense contractors on emerging metahuman contingencies. By the modern era he had attained flag rank as a General. ===Control=== He circulated among policymakers and defense-industry figures tied to the clandestine cabal Control, a coordination cell that attempted to steer superhuman outcomes through became known for covert procurement, deniable field assets, and influence operations. Within that circle he interfaced with General Edward Harrison, General Thaddeus E. Ross, General Cecil B. Slinkard, billionaire technologist Howard Stark, and robotics expert Dr. Bolivar Trask as Control shaped research pipelines and off-books budgets. When Control's capital streams were corrupted and siphoned into black projects that ultimately empowered threats such as Ultron and the Mad Thinker, the cabal fractured. ===Commission on Superhuman Activities=== The White House reassigned Haywerth into overt government channels as a senior military advisor to the Commission on Superhuman Activities so that his policy aims could continue under color of law with formal authorities over registration, contracting, and operational tasking. ===Project Homegrown=== From his Commission seat Haywerth was put in charge of the Weapon Plus program Project Homegrown as part of Weapon VII. They produced a Super-Soldier named Nuke who was controlled by specialist drug. He loaned Nuke to President Felix Caridad of Tierra Verde to suppress an insurrection, treating the operative as deniable outside U.S. borders. He later permitted the Kingpin to requisition Nuke for an assault on Daredevil in New York City, then moved to reclaim the asset after Daredevil's victory. During the attempted rehabilitation Nuke escaped Commission custody, rampaged, and was killed by federal fire despite efforts by Captain America and Daredevil to save him, drawing Rogers to confront Haywerth over the program's ethics and oversight. ===New Captain America=== Seeking alternatives to chemically unstable conditioning, Haywerth contracted Power Broker, Inc. to field-test a government superhuman codenamed G.I. Max. The trial ended with G.I. Max's death during a clash with Captain America, after which Haywerth joined the Commission in demanding Rogers appear before them and pressed the FBI to locate him for questioning. With Commission backing Haywerth asserted that the "Captain America" identity and equipment were federal property, demanding Rogers either accept direct oversight or surrender the mantle. Rogers relinquished the uniform and shield rather than serve as an instrument of policy. As Commissioners debated succession, Haywerth briefed them on super-soldier failures and the body selected John Walker as the new Captain America with Lemar Hoskins as Bucky. Haywerth monitored Walker's accelerated preparation alongside Douglas Rockwell and Val Cooper, then formally congratulated Walker and Hoskins on completing training. During the Commission's hardline phase Haywerth sanctioned sweeps that brought vigilantes such as D-Man, Diamondback, and Nomad into custody at Walker's hands. He observed as Rogers turned himself in to face federal charges only to be incarcerated by Commission order, further straining relations between federal managers and the hero community. As Walker's tenure grew volatile, Commission figures including Raymond Sikorski urged removing Walker and explored restoring Rogers to the role, a transition that only proceeded after Walker himself pressed Rogers to resume the mantle. ===U.S. Agent=== Working directly with Walker, Haywerth staged Walker's public death to create a deniable exit and refashioned him as "U.S. Agent". He authorized clinical alteration of Walker's memories to excise the trauma of his parents' murder, then later permitted a restoration while manipulating Walker's recollection so he believed he had requested the procedure. To unveil the rebranded operative, Haywerth arranged a live exercise with a Guardsman piloting Iron Monger Armor supplied via Stane International, using the spectacle to brief and win over the Commission to U.S. Agent's new identity. He attempted to retain "Battlestar" as a Commission asset, but Hoskins departed to investigate Walker's supposed demise. Maintaining Commission equities, Haywerth dispatched U.S. Agent to safeguard the Power Broker from an assassin later revealed as a Scourge operative, directing protection not only for a contractor but for the Commission's ongoing programs. He joined Commission votes to assign U.S. Agent to apprehend the Punisher, a mission complicated when U.S. Agent informally aligned with the vigilante against the Maggia. lewis milner.name: Lewis Milner
lewis milner.origin: Lewis Milner was the gym teacher at Citrusville High School where he targeted overweight student Edmond Winshed who died during practice on the school's running track. He too was accused by Alice Rimes during Edmond's funeral along with his entire family. The day after Alice's funeral she read Edmond's diary in the school office with the intention of publishing it in the yearbook. At the end of the diary, Alice had written an accusation aimed at Milner, where she described the last minutes of Edmond's life, with all the student witnesses, where Milner attacked Edmond and continued to make him run until his heart stopped. Wanting to eliminate evidence of her, Milner and Edmond's family captured Alice and attempted to force her to give them the combination to the safe where she had locked her diary. All this plethora of emotions meant that the Man-Thing intervened and went to the school gym where they kept Alice locked up and attacked everyone present, in particular he attacked Milner, initially burning his hands, fusing them together in a gesture of prayer and then taking him to the athletics track where Edmond had died and there he burned his heart killing him.

Years after Lewis Seaver was "erased," he was tracked down and killed by another test subject, Sebastian Derik.

leyla.name: Leyla
leyla.origin: Leyla was a Kurdish woman, who nevertheless used her talent for chemistry to work for the oppressive Iraqi regime. Despairing after her family and husband were killed anyway, she attempted to end her life by submerging herself in a river polluted with highly corrosive chemicals. The presence of an unknown organism allowed her to survive. In her new form, Leyla likened herself to the goddess Ishtar, using her talents for revenge; to this end, she gathered a band of followers around her and started a terror campaign. A group of insurgents used "Vitriol" as it was called - actually a weaponized bacterial strain which reproduced at an incredible rate, consuming iron and producing acid - against rival groups and the United States military in Iraq. Iron Man was dispatched to investigate her, but found that Vitriol could dissolve his armor. Analysis of Vitriol's composition revealed that she was covered with an acid-resistant micro-organism which protects her from her own biological weapons. When she planned to douse Baghdad with her deadly bacterium, destroying the city completely, Tony Stark had her bombed with a giant amount of magnesium hydroxide ("Milk of magnesia"), which neutralizes acid. She was not heard from again.
abilities: Leyla is a genius-level biochemist and geneticist.
weaknesses: Magnesium hydroxide - and theoretically any alkaline compound - can neutralize Vitriol's effects. Her destructive bacteria cannot penetrate force fields, or, presumably, any non-metallic material.

leyu yoshida.origin: ===Origins=== Leyu Yoshida was Shiro Yoshida's younger sister and just like was a mutant and had similar powers. ===Eve of Destruction=== Leyu's existence was unknown to the X-Men until she responded to Jean Grey's call for help after Professor X was captured by Magneto. Jean had expected Sunfire himself, but Leyu came instead. Possessed of an attitude similar to her brother's, she made her disdain for Jean's other recruits known immediately, yet for some reason joined the mission as Sunpyre. After Magneto's defeat, she returned to Japan and did not pursue further contact with the X-Men. ===X-Corps=== Months later, Sunpyre appeared as a member of the X-Corps, the militant mutant team run by Banshee, functioning as both an operative and as part of the "recruitment" program. She was working on stabilizing the powers of new recruit Abyss when she was attacked and seemingly killed by other members of the X-Corps, who were being controlled by Mastermind. Her legacy as Sunpyre was taken by an extra-dimensional being called Lumina, who joined Big Hero Six, a Japanese super-hero team. She was possibly later resurrected, as someone who looked just like her was seen along with other former X-Men and X-Men-related characters in Cyclops's Million Mutant March in Washington D.C.

lhok nor.name: Lhok-Nor
lhok nor.origin: Lhok-Nor was the chieftain of the Atlanteans. When offered to marry his daughter Sareena to King Kull as a mean to make peace between Atlantis and Valusia, Lhok-Nor first refused but finally accepted to let her meet with Kull, though rejected the idea of forcing Sareena to marry the Valusian king. Sareena and Kull did fell in love, but Sareena was assassinated in the City of Wonders during the wedding ceremony by a Wolf Man wearing the guise of an Atlantean wearing the guise of a Valusian nobleman. Lhok-Nor declared war to Valusia and attacked the capital, considering that Kull was responsible for her death and was blaming the Atlanteans in the place of his own countrymen. The Picts, led by their chieftain Taku, also attacked in retaliation for Valusia and Atlantis allying, in spite of Valusia being allied to them and of the eternal Pictish-Atlantean enmity. At the peak of the battle, Kull persuaded Lhok-Nor and Taku, to venture into the catacombs beneath the city and discover the real threat for the human race represented by the Wolf-Men. Moved by Kull's love for his daughter, Lhok-Nor agreed to help him defeat the Demonolater and ended the war. He proposed Kull to marry another of his daughters, but Kull refused, though encouraged him to let their people mingle to grow stronger against the treats humanity might be confronted to. Lhok-Nor was eventually eclipsed by Ku-Var, a more brutal overlord of Atlantis.

li pung.name: Li Pung
li pung.origin: Li Pung was a former Chinese military commander known as the “Butcher of Ah Loc,” a reputation earned during his service in Southeast Asia. During that period, he commanded troops that included Colonel Camden Leung, an officer who would later resurface in New York City. Li Pung’s wartime actions left deep scars, most notably on Rupert Duc, whose father was killed by forces operating under Li Pung’s command. Years later, Li Pung relocated to New York and established himself as the proprietor of the Golden Buddha restaurant. Despite presenting himself as a legitimate businessman, his past remained intertwined with criminal elements and old wartime secrets. His establishment became a target when members of the Savage Tigers—New York’s branch of the Hong Kong-based White Lotus Society—attempted to rob the restaurant. The attack resulted in multiple deaths and the kidnapping of his cook, known as Charlie. The Tigers were operating an illegal immigration racket, extorting payments from vulnerable immigrants. Charlie, who was in truth former Colonel Camden Leung, had been threatened for failing to comply with their demands. Leung also possessed knowledge of a 30-foot golden Buddha statue stolen from a Laotian temple by Chinese troops and smuggled into the United States. The statue became the focal point of a violent struggle between rival gangs. The Punisher intervened following the attack on the restaurant. In order to dismantle the Savage Tigers, he formed a temporary alliance with the Royal Cobras, a Vietnamese gang led by Rupert Duc—a man whose father had been killed under Li Pung’s command during the war. The conflict culminated in a dockside warehouse battle involving the Savage Tigers, the Seven Gates triad, and the Royal Cobras. During the firefight, Duc recognized Leung as one of the men responsible for his father’s death. After Leung was subdued by the Punisher, Duc executed him, fulfilling a long-standing blood oath. In the aftermath, Castle confronted Li Pung and warned him that he had twenty-four hours to return the stolen golden Buddha before the Royal Cobras came after him.

fields.history: Li Pung was a former Chinese military commander known as the “Butcher of Ah Loc,” a reputation earned during his service in Southeast Asia. During that period, he commanded troops that included Colonel Camden Leung, an officer who would later resurface in New York City. Li Pung’s wartime actions left deep scars, most notably on Rupert Duc, whose father was killed by forces operating under Li Pung’s command. Years later, Li Pung relocated to New York and established himself as the proprietor of the Golden Buddha restaurant. Despite presenting himself as a legitimate businessman, his past remained intertwined with criminal elements and old wartime secrets. His establishment became a target when members of the Savage Tigers—New York’s branch of the Hong Kong-based White Lotus Society—attempted to rob the restaurant. The attack resulted in multiple deaths and the kidnapping of his cook, known as Charlie. The Tigers were operating an illegal immigration racket, extorting payments from vulnerable immigrants. Charlie, who was in truth former Colonel Camden Leung, had been threatened for failing to comply with their demands. Leung also possessed knowledge of a 30-foot golden Buddha statue stolen from a Laotian temple by Chinese troops and smuggled into the United States. The statue became the focal point of a violent struggle between rival gangs. The Punisher intervened following the attack on the restaurant. In order to dismantle the Savage Tigers, he formed a temporary alliance with the Royal Cobras, a Vietnamese gang led by Rupert Duc—a man whose father had been killed under Li Pung’s command during the war. The conflict culminated in a dockside warehouse battle involving the Savage Tigers, the Seven Gates triad, and the Royal Cobras. During the firefight, Duc recognized Leung as one of the men responsible for his father’s death. After Leung was subdued by the Punisher, Duc executed him, fulfilling a long-standing blood oath. In the aftermath, Castle confronted Li Pung and warned him that he had twenty-four hours to return the stolen golden Buddha before the Royal Cobras came after him.

liam connaughton.name: Liam Connaughton
liam connaughton.origin: ===Origin=== Liam Connaughton was a young Northern Irishman living with his widowed mother on a farm ever since his father had been killed during an untold event related to the Irish conflict. He was living a happy and simple life there, engaging a romance with a girl named Bridget, whose dad had been killed along with Liam's. But his mutant power to generate massive explosions was emerging at the same period. ===Terrorists' weapon=== While the police were inquiring on what they thought were bombings, Bridget's brother Colin (a terrorist), made the connection between Liam and those explosions, having witnessed after one of them a perturbed Liam apologizing for it. He convinced his boss Seamus (friend to the deceased fathers of Bridget, Colin, and Liam) to use the boy, forcing him to perform terrorist acts against pro-conciliation events. But on the last planned attack, on a speech at church against civil war, both Liam and Colin rebelled against Seamus. Seeing his mother and Bridget looking for him, Liam exploded around himself, seemingly killing Seamus. He was arrested and declared dead, while Colin was incarcerated. The British Military, along with the Coalition government, agreed on the termination of Liam, judging him too dangerous for public safety. He was injected with Potassium chloride and seemingly died. However, it was revealed that he had been saved, and the program allowing that kind of operation was dismantled. thumb|left|270px|Liam meeting the Elizabeth II (Earth-616)|Queen ===Return=== He seemingly kept his powers after M-Day, and years later, he was among the British mutants invited by David Haller (Legion) to form a team to follow Xavier's dream. While Legion was making Wisdom thought they refused to cooperate in a complex manipulation, Lila Cheney came to Blindfold and Wisdom into the illusion to explain a false plan about them seemingly tearing apart Britain in order 'to wipe mutophobic Britain off the map", but it was revealed the whole plan was only constituted of good actions to prove the work of human-mutant coexistence. Liam's part of the plan was to meet Queen Elizabeth during a royal charity lunch, in order to prove that mutants were able to solve conflicts (the Northern Irish conflict here) without using violence or their powers.
powers: Explosions generation Energy blasts
weaknesses: Liam had very poor control over his abilities, and thus they could inadvertently manifest under stress. Later, he seemingly overcame that lack of control.
affiliations: Ally of Legion Formerly: an unnamed terrorist group

liam magill.name: Liam Magill
liam magill.origin: thumb|left|200pxLiam Magill was a young man from Belfast who was convinced that his brother Rory had been killed by the Black Hoods terrorists — who were actually men paid by Roxxon to exacerbate the conflict between the Ireland and the British governments in order to sell their weapons. He intended to avenge his brother personally. Later, Liam followed Peter Parker and Joy Mercado and managed to free them after they had been captured by the Black Hoods and taken to the Roxxon building. Captured by the Black Hoods along with Joy, they were both freed by Spider-Man, then Liam shot a Black Hood who was about to shoot Joy, but to his surprise, the Black Hood he shot was his brother Rory, who, on his deathbed, told him not to feel sorry for his actions as he had foolishly hired himself out just for money.

lian goh.name: Lian Goh
lian goh.origin: An undocumented Chinese immigrant, Lian Goh was trafficked into sex work, but managed to escape thanks to the aid of Ghost Rider, with whom she eventually fell in love. Sadly, her former enslavers managed to find her and killed her. She was then transformed into a Spirit of Vengeance named Pao Fu (after the Chinese goddess of vengeance) by Blackheart, who intended to use her in an elaborate plan to bond Noble Kale to his realm and thus gain access to Ghost Rider's power source. Though she retained her romantic feelings for Ghost Rider, she and her fellow Spirits of Vengeance overpowered him and took him to Blackheart's realm. There, Blackheart offered to break the curse on Kale's family, in exchange for Ghost Rider marrying Pao Fu and assuming control over the Spirits. He agreed, but asked to also marry Blackheart's consort, Black Rose, a reincarnation of Roxanne Simpson, the wife of former Ghost Rider Johnny Blaze. Blackheart agreed to this extra stipulation, intending for Black Rose to kill Ghost Rider. After the wedding, Kale was returned to Earth, while Ketch's soul was trapped within Blackheart's realm. Ghost Rider knew that Black Rose intended to kill him, and thus granted her and Pao Fu their freedom from Blackheart's control. As Kale's memories were restored, Ghost Rider grew stronger and slew Blackheart and took over his realm (after which he returned Ketch to Earth). Pao Fu played no role in Ghost Rider's subsequent reign, but apparently returned to Earth when Blackheart was revived, as she has appeared in S.H.I.E.L.D.'s files as an unknown quantity.
powers: Supernaturally-augmented abilities
weapons: Blade capable of killing other Spirits of Vengeance.

lian tang.name: Lian Tang
lian tang.origin: Lian Tang was a designer at the Shanghai branch of Parker Industries. She co-designed the latest Spider-Mobile with Peter Parker. While she and Peter were in an intimate relationship, she disapproved of Spider-Man's apparent insubordination, not knowing he and Peter are one and the same. She was in league with Scorpio, leader of the Zodiac, providing him with Parker Industries' security codes in exchange for medication for her mother, who was sick with cancer. When Scorpio threatened to have her disposed of as a loose end, she offered to kill Spider-Man for him in exchange for medication. She attempted to kill Spider-Man during Shen Quinghao's award ceremony, but couldn't go through with it. After learning the circumstances behind her attempted betrayal, Spider-Man forgave her and asked that she help him take Zodiac down. When Superior Octopus and Hydra targeted Parker Industries, Shanghai Branch, Lian Tang helped Spider-Man fight them off.

liana feeser.name: Liana Feeser
liana feeser.origin: Liana Feeser, like the other members of the Bastards of Evil, was kidnapped by the Superior and exposed to , in the process giving her incredible superpowers. She was also subjected to 'personal narrative implants', causing false memories. Among these was the belief that she had recently discovered that her true father was the supervillain the Grey Gargoyle. Taking on the codename "Mortar", she joined the the Bastards of Evil, believing in their mission of spreading wanton, purposeless destruction and terror. She was among the more laid back members of the group, though she often sided with Singularity in arguments. After Singularity revealed the truth and was killed by the Superior, she demanded to know the truth, only for her form to be used as a way to disable the Superior by Gravity long enough for the Young Allies to defeat the Bastards. Mortar, along with the remaining members of the Bastards of Evil, was then sent to prison. ===Lethal Legion=== Mortar presumably escaped prison somehow as she, along with a number of other second-rate supervillains, was recruited into Hank Pym's new anti-Ultron Lethal Legion.

lianda.name: Lianda
lianda.origin: Lianda was a Romani healer who operated from a small caravan in the nation of Wallachia during the mid 15th century. In the year 1459, Turkish warlord, Turac, brought the dying Wallachian prince, Vlad Dracul, to her carriage and told her to use her Romani magic to heal him. Like most Transylvanians, Lianda despised Turkish occupation and had no desire to see Dracula healed, only to become a puppet to Turac. What Turac never realized; however, was that Lianda was also a vampire. Guided by the commands of the ancient vampire, Varnae, Lianda drank the prince's blood until his human form died and he was reborn as a vampire. When Turac discovered Lianda's treachery, he impaled her with a silver-tipped spear. The wound, though severe, did not pierce her heart, and Lianda was able to shapeshift into a bat and fly away. She sought out Lord Varnae, and implored him to use his power to heal her. Varnae felt as if Lianda's usefulness was complete, so instead of healing her, he used his power to finish her off.
powers: Lianda possessed characteristics common to most vampires.
abilities: Lianda possessed a rudimentary knowledge of the occult.
weaknesses: Lianda was vulnerable to a stake through the heart. She presumably suffered from all the traditional weaknesses of a vampire.

libby windham.name: Libby Windham
libby windham.origin: Libby Windham was the wife of Reg Greenwood, with whom she had two daughters, Dawn and Eve. She suddenly left them one day, leaving Anchor Bay in a boat to San Francisco, leaving all of her belongings behind with a note that mentioned she desired more in her life, but was sorry nonetheless. Many years later, Dawn became the companion of the Silver Surfer. When she told him about her mother, the Surfer used his cosmically-empowered senses to track down Libby from a strand of hair left in a hairbrush, and flew with Dawn to San Francisco to have her reunite with Libby as a surprise. While initially reluctant to visit her estranged mother, Dawn nervously and knocked at her door. Dawn's presence surprised Libby, who received her daughter with coldness. Libby warmed up to Dawn as she told her mother about her adventures with the Silver Surfer. However, Libby abruptly kicked Dawn out of her house when she mentioned that Eve was pregnant. At that very same moment, the city was victim to an attack from Terra Forms, prompting Dawn to go help the Silver Surfer and Spider-Man fight them. During the battle, Dawn was partially drained of her life force by these creatures and her plasma levels reached dangerously low levels. Libby was present in the crowd when Spider-Man asked for a donor who shared blood type with Dawn, O negative. As she was losing consciousness, Dawn witnessed her mother backing down from going to her aid and disappearing into the crowd.

liberation mcallister.name: Liberation McAllister
liberation mcallister.origin: Liberation McAllister found interest in photography when he was young. Having fallen out of Sarah Lawrence College when he was nineteen, Liberation photographed bougie rock shows in New York City where fashion heiresses rubbed elbows with street punks. He photographed his first dead body at CBGB, where he discovered his true calling for morbid photography. Since many of the people at the shows he visited were models, he quickly moved to fashion photography. Liberation became popular for the way he set up photo shoots with a flippant environment, so fashion photography led to taking pictures of actors, tech moguls, and even presidents. At the same time he was taking over the art world in the public eye, Liberation started monopolizing a market behind the scenes, which he referred to as "snuff couture," taking pictures while killing unwilling models. This business made him a secret billionaire, and gained him entrance to the selective underground Société des Sadiques. The Société's biannual feast for new inductees was interrupted when Moon Knight revealed himself to have infiltrated the inner circle to hunt down the cult's leader Ernst. Moon Knight and the other inductees took part in four individual trials before fighting each other. For the fifth trial, Moon Knight brutally and effortlessly beat down the other contestants, including Liberation.

libertas.name: Libertas
libertas.origin: Libertas was a member of the Suffragists, the last remaining resistance to the Nazi zombie regime on Earth-12591. The Suffragists rescued the Ducky Dozen of Earth-616 from the zombified members of the Invaders, with Libertas incinerating Golden Girl with her torch. The Dozen had travelled to their world to stop the Nazi zombies from spreading their infection all over the Multiverse. To this end, the Suffragists took the Dozen back to their headquarters where they were introduced to Zephyr Zog, a Nazi scientist who wished to stop the zombie infection from spreading any further. The Suffragists accompanied Zog and the Dozen on their mission to wipe out the zombie threat. Libertas was killed alongside Flexo and the Blazing Skull by Thor's zombified goats.
powers: Libertas had the power of flight.
weapons: Libertas wielded a torch that was capable of shooting energy blasts that could incinerate a human being.

libra first sign.name: Libra (First Sign)
libra first sign.origin: The origins of this version of Libra are unknown but it's known they led a new Zodiac. The Zodiacs used a transformer to steal the power from Manhattan and used erecting an indestructible invisible shield around the city. The shield would allow the Zodiac to chart their own destiny by blocking out the stars and to rule the world. Captain America tracked down a squadron of Zodiacs, but was overwhelmed and fled to Avengers Mansion. The Zodiac chased him there and he found no one around so was again chased to the apartment of Thor and Amora the Enchantress. The Zodiacs were defeated and Amora learned of the dimensional portal they were using to enter Manhattan. They fled and were later confronted by Captain America, Thor and Iron Man at the transporter. A battle ensued and more Avengers were summoned to help. The battle lead to the Zodiacs' base aboard the Intrepid and Libra appeared and another battle ensued. Giant-Man located and destroyed their transformer, knocking out their shield and Libra and the Zodiac fled.

libra lmd.name: Libra (LMD)
libra lmd.origin: Libra was one of the Life Model Decoy created by Scorpio to serve as one of the members of his new Zodiac. He was forced to activate the LMDs early as a result of an attack by the Defenders. Libra chose not to fight against the Defenders, choosing instead to watch the battle from the sidelines. He chose to leave the battle before its conclusion, satisfied in the equality of the two sides. Later, Libra decided that the balance must be restored after Scorpio's defeat, so he decided to join Sagittarius in his criminal pursuits. They had watched Dollar Bill's documentary about the Defenders and learned that anyone who wanted to be considered a Defender could do so as a result of the team's non-team status. The two LMDs gathered a group of costumed super-villains and went on a rampage throughout New York City while calling themselves "Defenders". Libra took a group of these criminals to rob the New York Stock Exchange. Nighthawk met the villains at the exchange, but was quickly stopped, giving Libra and the others a chance to escape. Nighthawk and the rest of the Defenders met the group of villains at the docks. Libra had decided that order had been reestablished and disappeared, leaving the other villains to fight the Defenders. Libra was next seen when he joined the other members of the Zodiac and Quicksilver in opposing the Avengers. Libra, alongside Scorpio, Leo, and Virgo attacked the Keibler Circus, where they were opposed by the Avengers. As Libra harassed the circus' audience, Hawkeye destroyed him with a pair of rocket arrows. Scorpio recreated Libra using the Zodiac Key, transforming Libra into a new female form. This new version of Libra joined the other members of the LMD Zodiac in attacking the original Zodiac Cartel in Dallas, Texas. They succeeded in killing all of the original members with the exception of Cornelius van Lunt and took their places in the criminal underworld. The Zodiac next attacked a group of businessmen attending a cattle auction in Wichita, where they were met by the West Coast Avengers. Libra and Gemini both fought Mockingbird before fleeing when Sagittarius was destroyed by Hawkeye.
powers: Libra can fly and become intangible.

lichidus.name: Lichidus
lichidus.origin: Lichidus was an already powerful leader among his people, but he began using human sacrifices in attempts to gain dark power and ultimately became immortal, and gained the ability to manipulate water. He formed the Deathwalkers along with Cairn, Adur and Viciada, people with similar origins to his, and worked together to gain more power. Since old times, they tried to use the Talisman of Kamar-Taj to create a sacrifice so powerful it would destroy humanity. A failed attempt in 1908 caused the creation of The Bear. In 1972, one of their attempts to make the sacrifice was thwarted by the Mighty Avengers. The Talisman was taken from them and it was hidden in the Himalayas by Kaluu. The Talisman made its way to the Inhumans' Attilan. In the present times, the Deathwalkers returned to New York, and rediscovered the Talisman once Attilan fell on New York. Lichidus sent a hellhound to retrieve it, but if failed and Blade (who was undercover as Ronin) took it. The Deathwalkers then proceeded to send numerous creatures to fight the vampire slayer and get it. They finally succedeed in capturing Blade after sending Were-Roosters to battle him, and planned to use his blood for a sacrifice. Even though the Mighty Avengers located Blade and arrived to help him, the Deathwalker's legion of servants provided a distraction so the heroes couldn't get to Deathwalkers before they could finish their ritual. The successfully-finished ceremony merged them together into the Deathwalker Prime, a creature with control over the four elements, thus power over the fifth: the spirit, which would be the key for it to destroy humankind. However, the Mighty Avengers managed to get hold of the cup used in the ritual of merging, and using a similar procedure merged themselves into the Avenger Prime, which managed to destroy the Deathwalker Prime, mainly because unlike the Deathwalker, the different personas merged into it were truly spiritually bonded, while the personas composing the Deathwalker were fighting for control.
powers: Lichidus can control water. : His power over water allows Lichidus to use the water in living beings to control them. His influence is weaker the more distant he's from his target.
weaknesses: Sunlight: Direct exposure to sunlight can be lethal to Lichidus, even moonlight is irritant to them.

lickspit.name: Lickspit
lickspit.origin: Lickspit was a high-ranking member of the Warlord's army. He visited the Doka'abi Clan to investigate if they had found a champion to fight in their name in the Warlord's barbaric trials known as the Gauntlet. When the Doka'abi Clan called the Hulk for help, the Warlord tasked Lickspit with investigating how did they bring him through the Great Portal. Lickspit contacted a spy within the Doka'abi Clan, who provided him with the slab used by Maeera to send out the call for help. Lickspit intended to send another signal to the Earth and call the Hulk's enemies. Lickspit tested the strength of whatever creatures they brought from the portal by shooting them at sight. After failing multiple times to bring somebody strong enough, Lickspit succeeded when they pulled Odinson into Sakaar, whom Lickspit bent to his control using an Obedience Disk. However, while fighting Odinson, the Hulk managed to destroy the Disk and liberate him. At the beginning of the final round, in which the Hulk was set to confront the Warlord himself, Lickspit was still announcing the fight when the Warlord abruptly opened fire at the battleground, blowing Lickspit away into a cliff.

lieb lawson.name: Lieb Lawson
lieb lawson.origin: Prof. Lieb Lawson was an electrical engineer who attempted to harness electricity in new ways for the benefit of mankind. His experiments were financed by James Bennett and drew the attention of his ward, Madeline Joyce. When Lawson described that his experimental machine had briefly provided him with powers Joyce was fascinated by it and later that night during a large electrical storm she returned to his laboratory and used the machine. Lieb seeing his machine in use rushed to stop it but upon opening it discovered Joyce who he had assumed died. Distraught over what his machine had caused and that he was responsible he destroyed it and himself but Joyce somehow survived the ordeal albeit it after being in a coma for a week. Leib's machine had triggered her latent mutant powers which she used to fight crime and become the hero known as Miss America.

lieberman.name: Lieberman
lieberman.origin: Lieberman was one of S.H.I.E.L.D.'s newly recruited super-soldiers of the Reserves. Unlike the other Reserve members, who depend on using their costumes as the source of their powers (with the exception of the Goliaths), Lieberman's powers and abilities were completely innate, due to taking the Super-Soldier Serum. Lieberman was surprisingly briefed and shown by Nick Fury that he was potentially destined to replace Captain America if he ever died, or in some other cases in which Lieberman was very hesitant to fill in. On a night out with the Reserve members, Lieberman was involved in a fire scene and bravely rescued fifty-seven fire victims, but after saving them, he suddenly died. His body was taken back to the Triskelion and privately examined. The cause of his death was determined to be due to his nervous system collapsing from the strain of the Super-Soldier Serum. However, Lieberman's ascension to become (and replace) Captain America and his sudden death wasn't the first time that S.H.I.E.L.D. had tried to replicate super-soldiers like Captain America, and that several other candidates like Lieberman perished with similar results.
powers: Powers similar to Captain America, with a brain hardwired to S.H.I.E.L.D.'s super-computer.

lieutenant general fredricks.name: Lieutenant General Fredricks
lieutenant general fredricks.origin: Fredricks was a General in the United States Army. He had several run-ins with the X-Men early in the team's career. On occasion he was known to voice mild prejudice towards mutants. Fredricks once prevented his troops from firing their weapons at the Human Torch after the Torch had saved the army's atomic tank from the Miracle Man's monster. The Vanisher once threatened to steal continental defense plans from Fredricks. The villain later made good on that promise, only to have his attempt at blackmailing the government halted by the X-Men. After the X-Men defeated Bolivar Trask's Sentinels, Fredricks, on behalf of the armed services, thanked Charles Xavier for his aid as a civilian adviser. On orders from the Pentagon, Fredricks shot the experimental missile "Sonic Shark", that used cosmic energy, against the Silver Surfer, who had become a threat. The Fantastic Four diverted the missile to save the Surfer's life, which in turn convinced the Surfer to stop being a threat. Fredricks allowed the X-Men to confront Count Nefaria when he and his Ani-Men had taken control of NORAD at Valhalla Base. Fredricks had actually called for the Avengers, who were unable to make it. Later, still at Valhalla Base, General Fredericks was sufficiently concerned about tempests created by Storm to notify the President.

lifeforce.name: Lifeforce
lifeforce.origin: The mysterious woman known only as Lifeforce was a mutant member of the second incarnation of the Dark Riders. Her mutant ability enabled her to siphon the life out of any living creature and absorb the strength into herself. She was also well-trained in hand-to-hand combat. Along with the rest of the Dark Riders, her first mission was to hunt down mutants found unfit by their master, Genesis. The first target was the former Dark Rider, Foxbat. The Dark Riders tracked Foxbat down in Egypt and trapped him against the wall. Lifeforce asked her leader Gauntlet if she could "have" Foxbat, which he allowed. Lifeforce then killed Foxbat by draining his life from his body. Lifeforce and the Dark Riders were then ordered to hunt down Caliban, another of Apocalypse's former allies. They ambushed Caliban in the Morlock sewers in New York City where they encountered Cable, Domino, and Storm. Lifeforce brawled with Domino, and, getting the upper hand, began to drain Domino's energy. However, rubble from the falling debris hit Lifeforce in the back of the head, disorienting her and allowing Domino to headbutt the villain and escape her grasp. Her teammates grabbed Lifeforce and were teleported to safety by Hard-Drive. Caliban assisted the trio in tracking the Dark Riders to Egypt. Lifeforce ambushed Storm in the middle of the desert where Hurricane had created a sandstorm. Cable shot Lifeforce off of Storm before she could drain her. When Genesis appeared, the Dark Riders managed to capture Cable and take him to Apocalypse's old fortress. Cable's allies stormed the fortress and in the ensuing battle, Domino took out Lifeforce. Genesis, too, suffered defeat, and ordered Hard-Drive to teleport them to safety. Lifeforce was next seen threatening Mister Sinister alongside Genesis and the Riders. She later battled Jean Grey and began to drain Jean's consciousness from her physical body. Jean managed to fight Lifeforce off but soon found herself teleported away with the Dark Riders. In a Scotland castle dungeon, Lifeforce and her teammates Hurricane and Spyne freed the mutant Cyber from his imprisonment. They took Cyber to Akkaba where they met Jamil, a servant of Candra. Jamil led the Dark Riders to the Egyptian Citadel where Lifeforce tested his skills and reported back to Genesis. As Cyber started to suspect the Dark Riders of ill intent regarding his adamantium, he became aggressive. Lifeforce and her teammates restrained him and forced him into a chamber where he was attacked and killed by death-watch beetles, stripping his adamantium from his corpse. Jamil then led Wolverine to the Genesis's Citadel where he was captured by the Riders. Genesis planned to wipe Wolverine's mind and appoint him as his first Horseman. Lifeforce stood at the controls of the adamantium bonding apparatus. When Wolverine started rejecting the adamantium, Lifeforce used a fire extinguisher to clear the area and continue the process. However, the machinery overloaded and caused an explosion that killed Hurricane. Genesis ordered the other Dark Riders to chase after Wolverine, who had been rescued by Cannonball. When Lifeforce didn't respond to Genesis's orders, he moved her chair around to find that she, too, had been killed by the adamantium shrapnel. For unknown reasons, Lifeforce was the only Dark Rider not resurrected with the Transmode Virus by Selene.
powers: Lifeforce had the power to drain the energy from her victims by touch, revitalizing her own energy which could be fired in .
